ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r9.claim: The afterlife punishment is greater than worldly punishment and lasts because it does not end; al-Zamakhshari also compares permanent blindness with temporary hardship.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p394/r9.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى أن عذاب الآخرة أشد أي من عذاب الدنيا لأنه أعظم منه وأبقى

DURR-FULL:v5p610/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v5p610/r2.speaker: سفيان
DURR-FULL:v5p610/r2.claim: The one described as transgressing is a person who associated partners with God.
DURR-FULL:v5p610/r2.anchor: عن سفيان في قوله: {وكذلك نجزي من أسرف} قال: من أشرك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p69#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p69#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p69#2/r1.claim: The warning means that God similarly punishes those who exceed bounds and disbelieve.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p69#2/r1.anchor: وكما وصفنا من أليم الأفعال نجزي المسرفين المتعدين الكفار بالله عز وجل

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p69#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p69#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p69#2/r2.claim: If the constricted life is in this world or the barzakh, the verse adds an afterlife threat; if it is already in the afterlife, it reiterates that its punishment surpasses imaginable worldly pain.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p69#2/r2.anchor: إن كانت معيشة الضنك في الدنيا أو البرزخ فجاء هذا وعيدا في الآخرة بعد وعيد

JISHUMI:v7p4763/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4763/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4763/r1.claim: The preceding warning connects by analogy: as those turning away from the Qur'an were punished, so are those who commit excesses.
JISHUMI:v7p4763/r1.anchor: كما جزينا من أعرض عن القرآن كذلك نجزي من أسرف في المعاصي

JISHUMI:v7p4763/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4763/r2.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v7p4763/r2.claim: Abu Muslim says the account of Satan ends and the address turns to the Prophet and his community, applying the lesson from Adam and Satan to the Prophet's people.
JISHUMI:v7p4763/r2.anchor: وقيل: انقضت الحكاية عن مخاطبة إبليس وابتدأ مخاطبة النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:126-130/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:126-130/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:126-130/r2.claim: God gives the same punishment to those who commit excess by associating partners with him.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:126-130/r2.anchor: وكما نجزي من أعرض عن القرآن { نجزي من أسرف

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:126-130/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:126-130/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:126-130/r3.claim: The punishment of the afterlife is harsher and more lasting than worldly or grave punishment.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:20:126-130/r3.anchor: مما يعذبهم به في الدنيا والقبر

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p82/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p82/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p82/r3.claim: The word rendered as exceeding means to go beyond the limits.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p82/r3.anchor: The word إ means “to exceed the limits.”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p82/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p82/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p82/r4.claim: Those who exceed limits waste their talents on things they should avoid and neglect what they were required to do.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p82/r4.anchor: people who wasted their talents in the very things they had to abstain from

SAMIN-DURR:20:127/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:20:127/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:20:127/r1.claim: In the same way as that punishment, God punishes whoever exceeds the bounds.
SAMIN-DURR:20:127/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وكذلك نجزي من أسرف }: أي: ومثل ذلك الجزاء نجزي

ASAD-NOTES:20:122#n110/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:122#n110/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:122#n110/r1.claim: Asad cross-references his rendering of man asrafa to his discussion of musrif, a participial noun from the same root, in surah 10.
ASAD-NOTES:20:122#n110/r1.anchor: Regarding this rendering of the phrase man asrafa, see surah 10, note 21

ASAD-NOTES:20:127/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:20:127/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:20:127/r1.claim: God recompenses those who waste themselves and disbelieve in His messages with punishment in the life to come that is severe and enduring.
ASAD-NOTES:20:127/r1.anchor: and does not believe in his Sustainer's messages: and, indeed, the suffering

ALUSI-FULL:v16p279#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p279#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p279#2/r1.claim: The punishment is like-for-like with the offense: God punishes those who plunge into desires and disbelieve in, deny, or turn away from their Lord’s signs.

ALUSI-FULL:v16p279#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p279#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p279#2/r2.claim: The general class of punishment is compared with the specific punishment just described.
ALUSI-FULL:v16p279#2/r2.anchor: والمراد تشبيه الجزاء العام بالجزاء الخاص

ALUSI-FULL:v16p279#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v16p279#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v16p279#2/r3.claim: The hereafter’s punishment may mean punishment generally or specifically the Fire; it is harsher than the first punishment and lasts longer, or is harsher and more lasting than it, grave punishment, or resurrection blind.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p301#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p301#2/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p301#2/r4.claim: God similarly requites those who go beyond bounds by associating partners with Him and disbelieve in His signs; the afterlife punishment is harsher than worldly and grave punishment and lasts longer.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p301#2/r4.anchor: ولعذاب الآخرة أشد} مما يعذبهم به في الدنيا والقبر، {وأبقى} وأدوم.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:127/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:127/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:127/r1.claim: Excess means plunging into appetites and turning away from the signs.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:127/r1.anchor: بالانهماك في الشهوات والإعراض عن الآيات.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:127/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:127/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:127/r2.claim: Not believing the signs means denying them and acting against them.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:127/r2.anchor: بل كذب بها وخالفها. { ولعذاب الأخرة } وهو الحشر

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:127/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:127/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:127/r3.claim: The hereafter's punishment may mean resurrection while blind, or the Fire that follows.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:127/r3.anchor: وهو الحشر على العمى، وقيل عذاب النار أي وللنار بعد ذلك.

BAYDAWI-FULL:20:127/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:127/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:127/r4.claim: It is harsher and more lasting than straitened worldly life, or than that together with blindness; blindness may end in Hell so the person sees his place and condition.
BAYDAWI-FULL:20:127/r4.anchor: من ضنك العيش أو منه ومن العمى، ولعله إذا دخل النار زال عماه ليرى محله وحاله

BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r6.claim: The same severe recompense is given to one who exceeds bounds by following desire and arrogantly rejects God's commands, whether by denial or by acting like a denier.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r6.anchor: في متابعة هواه فتكبر عن متابعة أوامرنا

BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r7.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r7.claim: The punishment of the Hereafter, in whatever form, is harsher and more lasting than worldly punishment because this world is transient and a place of departure.
BIQAI-FULL:v5p55/r7.anchor: فإن الدنيا دار زوال , وموضع قلعة وارتحال

BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r1.claim: God gives a recompense corresponding to the offense.
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r1.anchor: {وكذالك} أي : ومثل ذلك الجزاء الموافق للجناية

BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r2.claim: Israf is exceeding the limit in any human action, though the term is most familiar in connection with spending.
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r2.anchor: والإسراف مجاوزة الحد في كل فعل يفعله الإنسان وإن كان ذلك في الإنفاق أشهر

BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r3.claim: The signs are the Qur'an and the other miracles, which the offender denied and turned away from.
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r3.anchor: أي : بالقرآن وسائر المعجزات بل كذبها وأعرض عنها

BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r4.claim: The phrase may refer to punishment in the Hereafter generally or specifically to the punishment of the Fire.

BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r5.claim: The afterlife punishment is more severe than worldly punishment such as constricted livelihood.
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r5.anchor: مما نعذبهم به في الدنيا من ضنك العيش ونحوه

BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r6.claim: The punishment lasts longer and does not end.

BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r7.claim: To escape punishment and gain reward, one should endure worldly hardships in obedience and avoid sins and worldly desires; Paradise is surrounded by hardships and Hell by desires.
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r7.anchor: فعليه أن يصبر على شدائد الدنيا في طاعة الله ويجتنب المعاصي وشهوات الدنيا فإن الجنة قد حفت بالمكاره وحفت النار بالشهوات

BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r8.claim: In a report, God sends Gabriel to inspect Paradise and then Hell; after each is surrounded respectively by hardships and desires, Gabriel fears few will enter Paradise and few will avoid Hell.
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r8.anchor: دعا الله جبريل فأرسله إلى الجنة فقال : انظر إليها وإلى ما أعددت لأهلها فيها فرجع فقال : وعزتك

BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r9.claim: A narration describes the people of Hell shackled and dragged face-down, struck by angels, and returned whenever they try to escape.
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r9.anchor: روي أن أهل النار إذا انتهوا إلى أبوابها استقبلتهم الزبانية بالأغلال والسلاسل

BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r10.claim: A hadith says the least punished person in Hell wears two sandals that make his brain boil.
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r10.anchor: وفي الحديث "إن أدنى أهل النار عذابا الذي يجعل له نعلان يغلي منهما دماغه في رأسه"

BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r11.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r11.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r11.claim: A sensible person should avoid the causes of punishment and blindness and strive not to be resurrected blind; separation from God, the Giver, is the most severe torment.
BURSEVI:v5p339#2/r11.anchor: وأشد العذاب عذاب القطيعة من الله الوهاب.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r1.claim: The passage uses three instances of ellipsis: the gathering also leaves the person forgotten, and the reply implies prior blindness to the signs as well as present blindness.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r1.anchor: وقد ظهر من نظم الآية أن فيها ثلاثة احتباكات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r3.claim: One reading makes this a continuation of God's rebuke to the person resurrected blind, with the conjunction linking it to the preceding sentence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r3.anchor: يجوز أن تكون من حكاية ما يخاطب الله به من يحشر يوم القيامة أعمى قصد منها التوبيخ له والتنكيل

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r4.claim: Alternatively, it is a closing lesson to listeners rather than part of the divine address, with the conjunction introducing a parenthetical conclusion to the story.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r4.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون تذييلا للقصة وليست من الخطاب المخاطب به من يحشر يوم القيامة أعمى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r5.claim: Here excess means false belief, disbelief, and stubbornly denying the Lord's signs.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r5.anchor: الاعتقاد الضال وعدم الإيمان بالآيات ومكابرتها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r6.claim: The comparison points to the narrow worldly life described for those who turn away: God gives the same kind of recompense to those who reject revelation.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r6.anchor: والمشار إليه بقوله { وكذلك } هو مضمون قوله { فإن له معيشة ضنكا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r7.claim: As a story conclusion, the afterlife punishment is contrasted with the worldly hardship of 20:124.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r7.anchor: ليس من حكاية خطاب الله للذي حشره يوم القيامة أعمى

IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r8.claim: Alternatively, God addresses the resurrected man: his afterlife punishment is worse and lasts longer than worldly punishment.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v16p332/r8.anchor: فالمراد بعذاب الآخرة العذاب الذي وقع فيه المخاطب ، أي أشد من عذاب الدنيا وأبقى منه لأنه أطول مدة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p332#3/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p332#3/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p332#3/r1.claim: The transgressor being punished here is one who committed shirk.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p332#3/r1.anchor: وكذلك أي وكما ذكرناه نجزي من أسرف أي اشرك

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p332#3/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p332#3/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p332#3/r2.claim: The hereafter's punishment is harsher than worldly or grave punishment and more enduring because it lasts.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p332#3/r2.anchor: ولعذاب الآخرة أشد من عذاب الدنيا ومن عذاب القبر وابقى لأنه يدوم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324#2/r1.claim: God requites profligate deniers of His signs in this life and the next, as also stated in 13:34.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324#2/r1.anchor: يقول تعالى: وهكذا نجازي المسرفين المكذبين بآيات الله في الدنيا والآخرة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324#2/r2.claim: The afterlife's punishment is more painful than worldly punishment and lasts longer; its people remain in it forever.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324#2/r2.anchor: أي: أشد ألما من عذاب الدنيا، وأدوم عليهم، فهم مخلدون فيه

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324#2/r3.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324#2/r3.claim: The Prophet told the spouses involved in mutual imprecation that the punishment of this world is easier than that of the next.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p324#2/r3.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم للمتلاعنين

JISHUMI:v7p4767/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4767/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4767/r1.claim: Punishment is recompense for deeds, against the compulsion doctrine; the verse also attributes extravagance to people themselves, unlike the claim that God creates it.
JISHUMI:v7p4767/r1.anchor: تدل الآية أن العقاب يقع جزاء على الأعمال خلاف قول المجبرة، لذلك قال: (وكذلك نجزي من أسرف)

JISHUMI:v7p4767/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p4767/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v7p4767/r2.claim: The reasoning also applies to children of polytheists, since they have no act of extravagance for which to be punished.
JISHUMI:v7p4767/r2.anchor: وكذلك في أطفال المشركين؛ لأنه لا سرف لهم

MUQATIL:20:126-127/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:126-127/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:126-127/r4.claim: The profligate meant here is one who associated partners with God in this life.
MUQATIL:20:126-127/r4.anchor: { وكذلك نجزي من أسرف } يعنى وهكذا نجزى من أشرك فى الدنيا بالنار فى الآخرة

MUQATIL:20:126-127/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:126-127/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:126-127/r5.claim: God's signs are the Qur'an, which the disbeliever did not believe.
MUQATIL:20:126-127/r5.anchor: { ولم يؤمن بآيات ربه } يقول: ولم يؤمن بالقرآن

MUQATIL:20:126-127/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:20:126-127/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:20:126-127/r6.claim: The afterlife punishment is worse than the worldly punishment of being killed at Badr and lasts longer; this warns Meccan unbelievers.
MUQATIL:20:126-127/r6.anchor: { ولعذاب الآخرة أشد } مما أصابه فى الدنيا من القتل ببدر { وأبقى } [آية: 127] يعنى وأدوم

NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#4/r1.claim: This is how God repays those who transgress and disbelieve His signs.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#4/r1.anchor: وكذلك نجزي من أسرف ولم يؤمن بآيات ربه

NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#4/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#4/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#4/r2.claim: After warning of constricted life and blind resurrection, the passage concludes that the lasting Hereafter punishment is harsher than temporary hardship in life.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p71#4/r2.anchor: لما توعد المعرض عن ذكره بعقوبتين المعيشة الضنك في الدنيا وحشره أعمى في العقبى

QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r8.claim: God likewise repays those who turn from the Qur'an and reflection on created things, and transgress the bounds through sin.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r8.anchor: وكما جزينا من أعرض عن القرآن، وعن النظر في المصنوعات، والتفكر فيها، وجاوز الحد في المعصية

QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r9.claim: Not believing in the Lord's signs means not affirming them as true.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r10.claim: The punishment of the Hereafter is more terrible than the constricted life and punishment of the grave.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r10.anchor: أي أفظع من المعيشة الضنك، وعذاب القبر.

QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r11.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r11.claim: The Hereafter's punishment is more enduring and stable because it never ends or ceases.
QURTUBI-FULL:20:125-127/r11.anchor: أي أدوم وأثبت لأنه لا ينقطع ولا ينقضي

QASHANI:20:124/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:20:124/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:20:124/r5.claim: The afterlife's punishment is harsher and more lasting than worldly constriction because it is spiritual and permanent.
QASHANI:20:124/r5.anchor: من ضنك العيش في الدنيا لكونه روحانيا دائما

RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r11.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r11.claim: One reported interpretation takes transgression to mean associating partners with God and unbelief.
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r11.anchor: اختلفوا فيه فبعضهم قال : أشرك وكفر

RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r12.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r12.claim: Another interpretation takes transgression to mean disobeying God.
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r12.anchor: وبعضهم قال : أسرف في أن عصى الله

RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r13.claim: The clause about not believing God's signs explains what is meant by transgression.
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r13.anchor: لأن ذلك كالتفسير لقوله : أسرف وبين أنه يجزي من هذا حاله

RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r14.claim: The afterlife punishment is harsher because of its magnitude and more lasting because it never ends.
RAZI-FULL:v22p113/r14.anchor: أما الأشد فلعظمه ، وأما الأبقى فلأنه غير منقطع

STUDYQURAN:20:124/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r9.claim: For the meaning of “the prodigal,” the commentary refers to 10:12.

STUDYQURAN:20:124/r10.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r10.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r10.claim: One interpretation is that perpetual afterlife blindness is more intense than any constriction experienced in worldly life.
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r10.anchor: The promise that the chastisement of the Hereafter is more severe and more lasting means that the disbeliever’s perpetual blindness in the Hereafter is more intense than any kind of constriction that he will experience in this life

STUDYQURAN:20:124/r11.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r11.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r11.claim: Alternatively, God's leaving the disbeliever blind in the Hereafter is more intense and lasts longer than the blindness caused by turning from God's signs.
STUDYQURAN:20:124/r11.anchor: Alternately, it can mean that God’s leaving the disbeliever in his state of blindness in the Hereafter is more intense and longer-lasting than the blindness that results from his turning away from God’s signs

TAB-FULL:v16p203#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p203#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p203#2/r1.claim: God requites those who transgress by disobeying Him and reject His messengers and books with the constricted grave-life described earlier.
TAB-FULL:v16p203#2/r1.anchor: وهكذا نجزي: أي نثيب من أسرف فعصى ربه، ولم يؤمن برسله وكتبه، فنجعل له معيشة ضنكا في البرزخ كما قد بينا قبل.

TAB-FULL:v16p203#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v16p203#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v16p203#2/r2.claim: The afterlife punishment is harsher than the grave's constricted life and lasts without an end.
TAB-FULL:v16p203#2/r2.anchor: يقول جل ثناؤه: ولعذاب في الآخرة أشد لهم مما وعدتهم في القبر من المعيشة الضنك {وأبقى} [طه: 71] يقول: وأدوم منها، لأنه إلى غير أمد ولا نهاية.

TABATABAI:20:127-129/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:127-129/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:127-129/r1.claim: The passage that follows gathers threats, promises, proofs, rulings, and consolation for the Prophet, all branching from the preceding discussion.
TABATABAI:20:127-129/r1.anchor: بيان متفرقات من وعيد ووعد وحجة وحكم وتسلية للنبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم متفرعة على ما تقدم

TABATABAI:20:127-129/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:127-129/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:127-129/r2.claim: Isrāf means going beyond the limit; the waw in “and thus” begins a new statement, pointing back to the punishment of those who turned away from remembrance and forgot God's signs.
TABATABAI:20:127-129/r2.anchor: الإسراف التجاوز عن الحد والظاهر أن

TABATABAI:20:127-129/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:127-129/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:127-129/r3.claim: Those who reject their Lord's signs exceed the bounds of servitude and receive the same recompense as those who forgot and abandoned the signs after being warned.
TABATABAI:20:127-129/r3.anchor: فإنه تجاوز منه عن حد العبودية وكفر بآيات ربه فجزاؤه جزاء من نسي آيات ربه

TABATABAI:20:127-129/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:20:127-129/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:20:127-129/r4.claim: The afterlife's punishment exceeds worldly punishment because it encompasses a person's inner and outer being and never ends.
TABATABAI:20:127-129/r4.anchor: أي من عذاب الدنيا وذلك لكونه محيطا بباطن الإنسان كظاهره ولكونه دائما لا يزول

TABRISI:20:126-129/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:126-129/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:126-129/r11.claim: God similarly requites those who associate partners with Him, exceed bounds in disobedience, and deny His proofs, scriptures, and messengers.
TABRISI:20:126-129/r11.anchor: أي وكما ذكرنا نجزي من أشرك وجاوز الحد في العصيان

TABRISI:20:126-129/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:20:126-129/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:20:126-129/r12.claim: The next life’s punishment is more severe than worldly and grave punishment, and more lasting because it never ceases.
TABRISI:20:126-129/r12.anchor: أي أدوم لأنه لا يزول وعذاب الدنيا وعذاب القبر يزول

THALABI:v6p265/r18.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p265/r18.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p265/r18.claim: Here excess means associating partners with God and disbelieving His signs; God punishes those who turn away in the same way.
THALABI:v6p265/r18.anchor: وكذلك أي وكما جزينا من أعرض وكذلك نجزي من أسرف أشرك ولم يؤمن بآيات ربه

THALABI:v6p265/r19.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p265/r19.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p265/r19.claim: The punishment of the afterlife is harsher than punishment in this life and the grave, and it is more enduring and established.
THALABI:v6p265/r19.anchor: ولعذاب الآخرة أشد مما يعذبهم به في الدنيا والقبر. وأبقى وأدوم وأثبت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p553#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p553#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس، الكلبي، أهل التفسير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p553#2/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Kalbī, and the exegetes say the person abandoned God's signs and did not believe; correspondingly, he is left in the Fire today.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p553#2/r2.anchor: هذا قول ابن عباس، والكلبي، وأهل التفسير

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p554/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p554/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p554/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses “whoever acted extravagantly” as one who committed shirk.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p554/r1.anchor: {وكذلك} كما ذكرنا {نجزي من أسرف} قال ابن عباس: (أشرك)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p554/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p554/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p554/r2.claim: The hereafter's punishment is more awful and greater than the grave punishment just mentioned; this supports reading the constricted life as punishment of the grave.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v14p554/r2.anchor: وهذا يدلس على أن المراد بقوله: {معيشة ضنكا}

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p290/r5.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p290/r5.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p290/r5.claim: The one who transgressed is a polytheist who wronged himself through associationism.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p290/r5.anchor: من أشرك، أسرف على نفسه بالشرك

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p290/r6.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p290/r6.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p290/r6.claim: The punishment of the hereafter is harsher than worldly punishment and never ends.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p290/r6.anchor: من عذاب الدنيا {وأبقى} [طه: 127] أي: لا ينقطع أبدا.
